youtube_title: Why Does the U.S. Have Time Zones? Blame the Railroads
youtube_description:
Why does the U.S. have time zones? Railroads created them on November 18, 1883, to replace clashing local times, and Congress made them law in 1918.

Before standard time, towns set clocks by the sun, and railroads ran on dozens of time standards. When the railroads switched to four zones across the continental U.S., clocks in the eastern part of each zone hit noon by the sun, were set back, and hit noon again: the Day of Two Noons.
